questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is considered the cause of the Triassic-Jurassic mass extinction about 201 million years ago?
options: Asteroid impact at Chicxulub with a global iridium anomaly and impact spherules
Rapid sea level fall that drained the continental shelves without any volcanism
76% species lost. CAMP volcanism (Central Atlantic Magmatic Province). Pangea breakup
Widespread continental glaciation with thick tillite sheets on every continent of Gondwana
questions.solution: Tr-J: allowed dinosaur dominance. CAMP: huge basalt flows. CO2 → warming → ocean acidification.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A peneplain landform represents which stage in the erosion of a landscape?
options: Initial stage of the geographic cycle of erosion
A lava plateau built by fissure eruptions
A coastal plain formed by sediment deposition
questions.solution: Peneplain: nearly flat surface near base level. End-cycle landscape of Davisian cycle. Almost at sea level.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Landsat 8 OLI bands: Band 4 (Red), Band 5 (NIR), Band 6 (SWIR1). NDVI formula:
questions.solution: NDVI: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index. Healthy vegetation: high NDVI (0.6-0.9).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Parasequences stack in which three patterns, progradational, retrogradational, and aggradational, distinguished by their trends?
options: Only progradational stacking that coarsens upward and shallows the basin, with no retrogradational or aggradational sets
Only retrogradational stacking that fines upward and never shallows the basin
Progradational (coarsening up, shallowing), Retrogradational (fining up, deepening), Aggradational (same facies)
Random stacking with no systematic relationship between successive parasequences
questions.solution: Parasequence: shallowing-upward cycle. Progradational: Parasequence sets thicken upward.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the hardness of the mineral calcite on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.solution: Calcite (CaCO3) — hardness 3. Scratched by copper coin. Effervesces in HCl.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Index minerals such as chlorite → biotite → garnet → kyanite → sillimanite mark increasing:
options: Sedimentary maturity of a clastic deposit through repeated reworking
Coal rank resulting from progressive burial and heating of organic matter
Intensity of chemical weathering in tropical humid climatic conditions
questions.solution: These index minerals appear at successive isograds, recording rising metamorphic grade.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The sudden appearance of abundant small shelly fossils and skeletonised marine animals around 541 Ma marks the beginning of which geological period?
questions.solution: Cambrian explosion: rapid diversification of shelly (skeletonised) metazoans at the Ediacaran-Cambrian boundary (~541 Ma), with small shelly fossils (SSF) at its base.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Alternating bands of normal and reversed magnetic polarity in oceanic crust flanking a mid-ocean ridge provide evidence for what process?
options: Symmetric pattern of normal/reversed polarity. Evidence for seafloor spreading
Stripes of alternating crustal thickness that record varying magma supply at the ridge
Pattern produced by the alignment of ferromagnetic minerals during regional metamorphism
Asymmetric zones of heat flow that record ridge propagation direction over millions of years
questions.solution: Vine-Matthews (1963): magnetic anomalies symmetric about ridge. Records geomagnetic reversals.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Wilson cycle describes the repeated opening and closing of which geological feature?
options: Opening and closing of ocean basins over geological time
Repeated subduction of oceanic lithosphere without rifting
Rifting of continents without subsequent ocean closure
Successive orogenic events unrelated to plate motions
questions.solution: Wilson: rift to ocean to subduction to collision to orogeny.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Index fossil criteria: short range, wide distribution, abundant, easily recognizable
options: Rare, long range, locally distributed, and difficult to identify in the field
Short range, wide distribution, abundant, easily recognizable
Local only. Restricted to one basin but spanning many successive stratigraphic stages
Long range, narrow distribution, scarce in outcrop and hard to tell apart from similar taxa
questions.solution: Index fossils: guide fossils. Used for biostratigraphic correlation. E.g., graptolites, ammonites, trilobites.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The extinction of the non-avian dinosaurs at the K-Pg boundary is attributed to which cause?
options: Gradual climate cooling across the entire Mesozoic
Widespread disease among large terrestrial animals
A single eustatic sea level regression event
questions.solution: K-Pg: asteroid impact (iridium anomaly, shocked quartz) + Deccan Traps. Ended Mesozoic Era.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mineral processing: froth flotation reagents:
options: Frothers, because generating stable bubbles alone is sufficient to float minerals
Collectors, which by themselves render every mineral surface hydrophobic
No chemical reagents are needed, as minerals separate by their intrinsic wetting
questions.solution: Collector: renders mineral hydrophobic. Frother: stabilizes bubbles. Depressant: prevents flotation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A significant shift in the carbon isotope ratio δ13C recorded in sedimentary rocks is interpreted as evidence of what?
options: Changes in surface temperature of the oceans alone
Changes in atmospheric pressure over the continents
The lithology of the host rock with no carbon involved
questions.solution: δ13C: fractionation by photosynthesis. Excursions indicate mass extinctions, methane release, or organic carbon burial.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Skarn, a Ca-Fe-Mg silicate rock of contact origin, is important economically because it hosts what?
options: Hydrothermal quartz veins that carry gold, silver and base-metal mineralization
Regional metamorphic rock that is characteristically rich in garnet, kyanite and sillimanite
Felsic volcanic rock formed by explosive eruption of intermediate andesite magma
Ca-Fe-Mg silicate rock. Contact metamorphic/metasomatic. Ore deposits (W, Cu, Fe)
questions.solution: Skarn: carbonate rock altered by intrusion. Pyroxene, garnet, wollastonite. Tactite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A glomeroporphyritic texture in an igneous rock indicates which process during crystallization?
options: Rapid quenching of lava at the surface
Mixing of two contrasting magma batches
questions.solution: Glomeroporphyritic: clusters of phenocrysts. Crystal mush accumulation, or synneusis (clumping in melt).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Magnetostratigraphy: normal polarity = same as present field. Reversed:
options: Magnetic minerals aligned in the same direction as the present-day field
Magnetic minerals aligned opposite to present field direction
No alignment of magnetic grains because the rock is fully non-magnetic
Random orientation of magnetic grains due to post-depositional reworking
questions.solution: Geomagnetic polarity time scale (GPTS). Cande and Kent (1995). Chron boundaries.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A wave-cut platform at the base of a sea cliff is formed by which process?
options: Wave erosion at base of cliff
Deposition of sediment by a graded river
Abrasion beneath an advancing ice sheet
Deflation of fine material by prevailing wind
questions.solution: Wave-cut platform: horizontal rock surface at base of sea cliff, formed by wave abrasion. Retreating cliff leaves platform.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which parameters are used in Bieniawski's Rock Mass Rating (RMR) system?
options: Barton. UCS × RQD × joint spacing × condition × groundwater
Bieniawski. UCS + RQD + joint spacing + condition + groundwater
Only UCS and RQD with no joint or groundwater parameters at all
Only the condition of joints, ignoring all strength parameters entirely
questions.solution: RMR: sum of 5 parameters. Class I (81-100, very good) to V (<20, very poor).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Shear sense indicators — sigma (σ) porphyroclast:
options: Mica fish with asymmetric tails that record the shear sense
Tails at angle to foliation. σ_a (asymmetric tails on both sides) and σ_c (tails in pressure shadow)
Delta porphyroclast with curved recrystallized tails that spiral completely around the rigid central grain
S-C fabric with oblique schistosity and discrete shear bands
questions.solution: σ: tails parallel to shear direction. σ-type: tails merge in matrix. δ-type: tails embayed.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes sea-floor spreading and the evidence recorded as magnetic striping?
options: The oceanic crust is oldest at the crest of the mid-ocean ridge and becomes progressively younger away from it
Mid-ocean ridges create new oceanic crust. Magnetic striping (Vine-Matthews). Age increasing from ridge
The oceanic crust has the same age everywhere on the sea floor regardless of the distance from the spreading ridge axis
Oceanic crust age varies randomly with distance from the mid-ocean ridge axis showing no systematic pattern at any spatial scale of measurement
questions.solution: Spreading rate: slow (1-2 cm/yr, Mid-Atlantic), fast (5-10 cm/yr, East Pacific Rise).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ocean island basalt (OIB) associated with plumes shows light REE enrichment and high Sm/Yb; these features indicate what about its source?
options: Enriched mantle (primitive + subducted). (La/Sm)_N > 1. Garnet in source → high Sm/Yb
Arc basalt formed by flux melting of the mantle wedge above a subducting oceanic slab
Depleted mid-ocean ridge basalt source with (La/Sm)_N < 1 and low Sm/Yb ratios
Depleted mantle that has undergone extensive melt extraction at a ridge
questions.solution: OIB: Hawaii, Iceland. Pb-isotope: HIMU, EM1, EM2 mantle components. High ³He/⁴He.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifuge is a geological unit that neither contains nor transmits groundwater because it is completely impermeable, such as:
options: A unit that stores water but transmits it only very slowly
A porous unit that yields water under the influence of gravity
A unit whose permeability is high in all three directions
questions.solution: Aquifuge: no primary porosity, no secondary porosity. No water.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Miller-Bravais indices (hkil) for hexagonal system:
options: 2-index notation, using only the a-axis and c-axis intercepts
5-index notation, adding a redundant axis to describe faces
3-index only. The hkl scheme fully describes hexagonal faces without i
questions.solution: 4-index: h, k, i=-(h+k), l. {10-10} = prism face. {0001} = basal pinacoid.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which mineral assemblage is characteristic of the greenschist facies of regional metamorphism?
options: Olivine, clinopyroxene, plagioclase and spinel (ultramafic assemblage)
Glaucophane, lawsonite, jadeite and aragonite (blueschist assemblage)
questions.solution: Greenschist: 300-500C, low-medium P. Greenschist facies: green minerals. Basalt composition.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which option correctly describes a drumlin, its composition and the orientation of its ends?
options: Ridge of stratified sand and gravel deposited by a stream beneath the glacier
Ridge of unsorted debris dumped along the margin of a glacier during retreat
Steep-sided mound of stratified drift deposited at the edge of the melting glacier
Streamlined glacial till hill. Stoss (steep) end up-ice, tail down-ice
questions.solution: Drumlin: ice flow direction indicator. Swarm: 'basket of eggs' topography.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 100 m on flat ground and dips at 50°. Its true thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 100×sin50° ≈ 76.6 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Moho discontinuity, marking the base of the crust, lies at what depths beneath oceanic and continental crust?
options: 100 km. A uniform depth beneath oceans and continents, coincident with the top of the asthenosphere
2 km. The shallow depth at which the Conrad surface truncates the continental upper crust
~5-10 km (oceanic), ~30-50 km (continental). Base of crust. Seismic P-wave jump ~6.7→8.1 km/s
10 km everywhere. S-wave velocities drop sharply below this universal crustal base
questions.solution: Moho: crust-mantle boundary. Defined by Vp. Faster in mafic lower crust.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In vertical electrical sounding (VES), increasing the current electrode spacing has what effect, and what earth model is assumed?
options: Both current and potential electrodes moved together along a fixed survey profile line
Current electrode spacing increased → probes deeper. 1D layered earth model
Keeps all electrode spacings constant and stacks readings at each station for noise
Profiles along a line at constant spacing to map lateral resistivity changes only
questions.solution: VES: Wenner or Schlumberger. AB/2 increases → deeper. Curve matching or inversion.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do large igneous provinces like the Deccan and Siberian Traps represent?
options: Slow cooling of magma in large plutons accompanied by extensive mineral layering
Explosive eruptions that build steep-sided stratovolcanoes of andesitic composition
Small volume eruptions confined to isolated vents along a spreading ridge
Large igneous provinces (LIPs). Deccan, Siberian Traps. Columnar jointing
questions.solution: Flood basalt: fissure eruptions. 10³-10⁶ km². Some linked to mass extinctions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is the birefringence of a mineral defined in optical mineralogy?
options: Sum of the principal refractive indices of a crystal
Difference between highest and lowest refractive index
Average refractive index measured along the optic axis
Product of the refractive indices along two vibration directions
questions.solution: Birefringence = nγ - nα. Calcite: 0.172 (very high). Quartz: 0.009 (low).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What distinguishes joints from faults, and how do systematic joints differ from non-systematic joints?
options: Fractures along which measurable displacement always occurs parallel to the walls
Fractures with no displacement. Systematic (parallel) vs non-systematic
Fault surfaces on which the hanging wall has moved relative to the footwall block
Folds produced by regional compression acting perpendicular to the bedding planes
questions.solution: Joints: cooling (columnar), tectonic (shear, extension), unloading (exfoliation).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mantle minerals: ringwoodite in transition zone (410-660 km):
options: Low-pressure. It is the stable form of olivine at ambient surface conditions
Spinel structure, (Mg,Fe)₂SiO₄. High-pressure polymorph of olivine
Only olivine composition. No iron substitution or structural change occurs with depth
At surface. It crystallises in basalts during rapid cooling at the Earth's surface
questions.solution: Ringwoodite: spinel structure. 520 km discontinuity. Ringwoodite inclusions in diamond: water.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which property makes a fossil a good index fossil?
options: Restricted to igneous rocks and giving a reliable absolute age for the enclosing pluton
Short geological range plus wide geographic distribution
Found only locally within a single sedimentary basin of unknown stratigraphic position
Long geological range coupled with a narrow geographic distribution in deep-water facies
questions.solution: Brief existence pins a narrow time; wide spread allows correlation across regions.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Electron spin resonance (ESR) dating works by measuring trapped electrons in which materials, and over what age range?
options: U-Pb method applied to uranium-bearing minerals of the sedimentary deposit being studied, for very old samples
Trapped electrons in tooth enamel, calcite, quartz. Range: few ka to ~2 Ma. Non-destructive
OSL method on quartz and feldspar grains from the same depositional unit of sediment
C-14 method on organic remains and charcoals of recent geological age and origin
questions.solution: ESR: detects unpaired electrons. Used for fault gouge dating. Combined ESR + U-series.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In apatite fission track analysis, tracks anneal over what temperature range that defines the partial annealing zone?
options: Tracks remain stable at room temperature over geological time spans
Tracks anneal only above five hundred degrees centigrade at any depth
Tracks never anneal under any combination of temperature and time
Tracks anneal at ~60-120°C. Partial annealing zone (PAZ): 60-120°C
questions.solution: Apatite FTT: thermochronometer. Tracks stable <60°C. Fully annealed >120°C. Track length analysis.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The decay of ⁸⁷Rb to ⁸⁷Sr forms the basis of which radiometric dating technique, and what is the stable radiogenic daughter isotope?
questions.solution: Rb-Sr dating: ⁸⁷Rb (T½ ~49 Gyr) β-decays to ⁸⁷Sr; isochron method plots ⁸⁷Sr/⁸⁶Sr vs ⁸⁷Rb/⁸⁶Sr. Used to date whole rocks and minerals older than ~3.5 Ga.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: After 4 half-lives, the percentage of the original radioactive parent isotope remaining is:
questions.solution: Fraction remaining = (1/2)^4 = 6.25%.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What are the principal limitations of the radiocarbon (C-14) dating method?
options: Applicable to any type of geological material regardless of the age involved
Limited to organic material up to ~50,000 years; requires calibration
No calibration curve is needed for the measured radiocarbon ages at all
Applies to rocks of any age, ancient or very young alike, without limit
questions.solution: C-14: T½=5730 years. Effective ~50ka (8 half-lives). Calibration: IntCal20. AMS for small samples.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The formation of a normal fault is mainly attributed to which type of tectonic stress?
options: Compressional stress that shortens the crust and thickens it
Shear stress oriented parallel to the fault plane at a shallow angle
Hydrostatic pressure acting equally in all directions at depth
questions.solution: Tension drops the hanging wall down relative to the footwall — a normal fault.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The progressive transformation of plant matter into higher-rank coal is called:
questions.solution: Coalification increases carbon and reduces moisture/volatiles as burial heat and pressure rise.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An aquifer (K = 25 m/day) of cross-section 500 m² has a hydraulic gradient of 0.01. The groundwater discharge is about:

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the hardness value of talc on the Mohs scale of mineral hardness?
questions.solution: Talc (Mg3Si4O10(OH)2) — softest mineral. Diamond = 10.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Elevated wave-cut platforms along a coast are correlated with which events in the past history of sea level?
options: Marine terraces are correlated using only the measured rate of tectonic uplift
The terraces have random elevations that cannot be correlated between different locations
Elevated wave-cut platforms. Correlated with sea-level highstands (MIS stages)
Terraces at different locations cannot be correlated by any method available to geologists today
questions.solution: Terraces: marine isotope stages. MIS 5e (125ka) is well preserved. Tectonic uplift rate calculation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a digital elevation model with 30 m resolution, what ground area does each grid cell represent?
options: Vertical accuracy of the elevation model is 30m
Total horizontal coverage of the scene is 30m
questions.solution: DEM: elevation values in grid. 30m = horizontal resolution.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is Rock Quality Designation (RQD) computed from intact core recovery?
options: Length of all recovered pieces divided by the drilled hole depth
Number of fractures counted per metre of recovered drill core
Total core recovery percentage including all broken fragments
questions.solution: RQD: sum of pieces >100mm/total core length × 100. Rock mass classification.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What process removes early-formed crystals from a melt, changing magma composition?
options: Early-formed crystals removed from melt, changing magma composition
Mixing of two magmas of different composition to yield an intermediate blend
Partial melting of the source that leaves a refractory residue behind
Assimilation of country rock into the melt without any crystal separation
questions.solution: Bowen's series: early olivine settles, residual melt becomes more felsic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What event does the term 'Cambrian explosion' describe in the history of life?
options: Triassic recovery of fauna after the great end-Permian mass extinction event
Precambrian radiation of soft-bodied Ediacaran organisms in the Vendian
Permian diversification of reptiles across the supercontinent Pangaea
Rapid appearance of major animal phyla (~541 Ma). Burgess Shale (507 Ma)
questions.solution: Burgess Shale (Canadian Rockies): exceptional preservation (soft parts). Trilobites, brachiopods.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What types of sediment accumulate slowly in the deep open ocean as pelagic deposits?
options: Biogenic ooze (calcareous/siliceous) and red clay. Slow accumulation
Glacial deposits of till and outwash transported by ice sheets to the sea
Aeolian sand dunes and loess deposited by wind in arid continental interiors
Terrigenous clastics derived from continents and deposited on shelves and slopes
questions.solution: Calcareous: foraminifera, coccoliths. Siliceous: radiolaria, diatoms. CCD controls carbonate preservation.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Eclogite is a very high-pressure rock, notable as the densest crustal rock, composed of which minerals?
options: Low-pressure rock that contains cordierite and andalusite minerals
Very high P. Garnet + omphacite (sodic pyroxene). Density ~3.5 g/cm³
Quartz-rich rock with abundant feldspar and biotite that formed at shallow depth
Hornblende-bearing rock that formed at medium metamorphic grade and pressure
questions.solution: Eclogite: basaltic composition at >12 kbar. Density similar to mantle.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The neutron (CNL) logging tool measures hydrogen index to estimate porosity, and a gas crossover with the density log indicates:
options: Formation bulk density from Compton scattering and photoelectric absorption index of the matrix
Compressional slowness used to derive porosity with the Wyllie time average equation
Natural gamma activity of potassium, uranium and thorium for shale volume estimation
Hydrogen index → porosity. Water-filled pores. Log overlay for gas (gas crossover with density)
questions.solution: Neutron: Am-Be source. Thermal neutron capture. Shale: high neutron porosity (bound water).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Mineral exploration: geophysical methods for base metal exploration:
options: No geophysical method can detect base-metal sulfides beneath conductive overburden
EM (electromagnetic) methods detect conductive massive sulfides
Gravity methods, because sulfide orebodies lack any magnetic or electrical response
Magnetic methods, as all base-metal sulfides are strongly ferrimagnetic
questions.solution: EM: time-domain or frequency-domain. Massive sulfides: good conductors. Detectable at depth.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In accuracy assessment of a classified satellite image, which statement about the Kappa coefficient is correct?
options: It measures only the producer's accuracy of a single land-cover class
It measures agreement between the classified map and ground truth after correcting for chance agreement
It is numerically identical to the overall accuracy for every confusion matrix
It is computed only for unsupervised classification outputs
questions.solution: Kappa (κ) = (observed agreement − chance agreement)/(1 − chance agreement), computed from the error/confusion matrix. κ > 0.8 indicates strong agreement; it corrects for agreement that would occur by chance.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a dip-slip fault, movement occurs along which direction, and what are the two resulting fault types?
options: Movement along the strike direction with no vertical component involved
Pure rotational movement about a vertical axis with no translation at all
Movement along dip direction (normal or reverse)
Oblique movement combining equal strike and dip components on the fault
questions.solution: Dip-slip: vertical component. Oblique-slip: both dip and strike components.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: An opencast block of 50000 m² has 50 m of overburden above the seam. The overburden volume to be removed is:
questions.solution: Volume = area × depth = 50000×50 = 2500000 m³ = 2.5 million m³.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Evaporation is measured with a Class A evaporation pan and converted to lake evaporation using:
options: Class A evaporation pan. Pan coefficient (0.7-0.8) to convert to lake evaporation
Direct measurement of the total volume of water lost from the surface of the lake by evaporation
Pan evaporation readings that require no conversion factor of any kind to be applied
Measurement of the evaporation losses using a standard recording rain gauge instrument
questions.solution: Class A pan: 1.2m diameter, 0.25m deep. Pan evaporation > lake evaporation (K_p).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In rock mass classification, the Geological Strength Index (GSI) estimates which property used as input to the Hoek-Brown failure criterion?
options: Rock mass quality based on blockiness and joint surface condition
Porosity of the intact rock material
questions.solution: GSI (Hoek-Brown criterion) estimates rock mass strength from the structure (blockiness) and joint surface condition; it correlates with RMR and Q systems and is used with the Hoek-Brown failure criterion for slopes and tunnels.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Convergent, divergent and transform plate boundaries represent which classification of interactions between lithospheric plates?
options: Plate boundaries consist only of convergent margins where plates collide with one another
Plate boundaries consist only of divergent margins where plates move apart from one another
Plate boundaries consist only of transform margins where plates slide horizontally past one another without creating or destroying crust
questions.solution: Tectonic plates: 7 major (Pacific, N.Am, S.Am, Africa, Eurasia, Australia, Antarctica). Move cm/yr.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) in remote sensing:
options: Increases the number of bands by creating additional synthetic channels of data output
Reduces correlated bands to uncorrelated components. PC1 = maximum variance
Adds false colour composites to the image, in order to improve the visual interpretation of it
Simply reorders the original bands, without changing any of their numerical values at all
questions.solution: PCA: dimensionality reduction. PC1: brightness. PC2: contrast. PC3: noise usually.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following is a typical stratabound, carbonate-hosted Pb-Zn deposit formed by warm basinal brines?
questions.solution: MVT deposits: stratabound Pb-Zn hosted in carbonate platforms, precipitated by warm basinal brines (e.g., Zawar, Rajasthan). SEDEX deposits are similar but synsedimentary and hosted in shale.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sequence records oceanic crust: peridotite, gabbro, sheeted dykes, pillow basalt, chert?
options: Continental crust section composed of gneisses, schists and granite plutons beneath mountain belts
Granite batholith with its associated pegmatite and aplite dyke swarms
Volcanic arc sequence built of andesite lavas and pyroclastic deposits
Oceanic crust sequence: peridotite → gabbro → sheeted dykes → pillow basalt → chert
questions.solution: Ophiolite: obducted oceanic lithosphere. Troodos (Cyprus), Oman.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Geological time scale divisions (largest to smallest):
options: Only the two finest divisions, Epoch and Age, are formally recognised
Age, Epoch, Period, Era, Eon when arranged from the smallest to the largest
Random order that varies from one geological region to another in the world
questions.solution: Eon: Precambrian, Phanerozoic. Era: Paleozoic, Mesozoic, Cenozoic. Period: Cambrian, etc.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How is porosity in sedimentary rocks classified, and what processes generate each type?
options: Porosity related only to the size and shape of sedimentary structures
Only secondary porosity, with all primary depositional porosity completely absent
Only primary porosity, with no secondary dissolution or fracture porosity present
questions.solution: Sandstone: intergranular porosity. Carbonates: vuggy, moldic, fracture porosity.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Well log correlation: gamma ray log identifies:
options: Porosity from the neutron hydrogen index at any depth
Fluid resistivity and water saturation of the logged interval
Matrix density and acoustic travel time for secondary porosity
Shale content (high GR = shale, low GR = sand/carbonate)
questions.solution: GR: natural radioactivity. K, U, Th. Shale: high GR. Sand: low GR. Clean carbonate: low GR.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A dipping coal seam outcrops over a horizontal width of 50 m on flat ground and dips at 50°. Its true thickness is about:
questions.solution: True thickness = horizontal width × sin(dip) = 50×sin50° ≈ 38.3 m.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In the Jacob straight-line method of aquifer test analysis, drawdown is plotted against log time on:
options: Match the observed field data to a type curve of W(u) against the 1/u values
Bouwer-Rice analysis of slug recovery for the same test data set
Hvorslev analysis of the initial water level in the observation well of the test
questions.solution: Jacob: t₀ from s=0 intercept. T = 2.303Q/(4π·Δs). S = 2.25T·t₀/r².

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Natural levees, backswamps, oxbow lakes, yazoo streams and crevasse splays are characteristic features of which environment?
options: The floodplain contains only natural levee deposits along the banks
The floodplain contains only abandoned meander loops or oxbow lakes
The floodplain contains only crevasse splays formed during major flood events
Natural levee, backswamp, oxbow lake, yazoo stream, crevasse splay
questions.solution: Floodplain: flat area adjacent to river, periodically flooded. Alluvial soil.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is an intrusive igneous body smaller than a batholith (<100 km²)?
options: Igneous body that is exactly the same size as a batholith in outcrop area
Intrusion larger than a batholith extending over hundreds of square km
Volcanic landform built of lava flows and pyroclastic material around a vent
questions.solution: Stock: similar to batholith but smaller. Often associated with mineral deposits.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which sequence correctly shows the progressive metamorphic grade sequence for pelitic rocks?
questions.solution: Increasing T/P. Slate (low), phyllite (sheen), schist (crystals visible), gneiss (bands).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Evapotranspiration is the combined process of water loss from the soil and vegetation, and its reference rate (ETo) is estimated from:
options: The loss of water only from the surface of open water bodies and bare soil
Combined evaporation + transpiration. Reference ET (ETo) from weather data
The release of water vapour only through the leaves and stomata of plants
The downward movement of water through the soil profile into the groundwater table below
questions.solution: Penman-Monteith: ETo = (0.408Δ(R_n-G)+γ·900/(T+273)u₂(e_s-e_a))/(Δ+γ(1+0.34u₂)).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: How do stone columns improve the engineering behaviour of soft ground?
options: Cement grouting of the soil to form a rigid continuous mass beneath the structure
Vibro-replacement. Granular columns improve bearing capacity and drainage
Soil nailing of the slope face without any ground densification
Deep mixing with lime slurry to stabilize the entire soil layer
questions.solution: Stone columns: 0.6-1.1m diameter. Install by vibroflot. Reduce liquefaction. Increase BC 2-3×.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Arranged from lowest to highest rank, the coal series is:
questions.solution: Increasing rank (carbon content) goes peat, lignite, sub-bituminous/bituminous, anthracite.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the seismic refraction method primarily used to determine?
options: S-wave velocity of the deeper mantle beneath the continental crust
Electrical conductivity to locate ore bodies and mineral veins
Magnetic anomalies produced by the iron-rich rocks below
P-wave velocity. Depth to bedrock, rippability
questions.solution: Seismic: hammer or explosives. Higher Vp = harder rock. Refraction for shallow (<30m).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A 3 m seam over 6 km² (density 1.4 t/m³) has a recovery factor of 0.75. The mineable reserve is about:
questions.solution: Mineable = area×thickness×density×recovery = 6M m²×3×1.4×0.75 ≈ 18.9 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In tectonic stress analysis, what do the three principal stress symbols σ₁, σ₂ and σ₃ respectively represent?
options: σ₁ < σ₂ < σ₃, with σ₃ representing the maximum principal stress in the system
σ₁ = σ₂ = σ₃, so stress is equal in all directions and no shear acts on any plane
σ₁ = σ₃ at failure, so the two horizontal stresses are always equal in value
σ₁ > σ₂ > σ₃. Maximum, intermediate, minimum principal stresses
questions.solution: Anderson: σ₁ vertical (normal faults), σ₂ vertical (strike-slip), σ₃ vertical (thrust).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Using a simplified proxy where calorific value ≈ 70 × fixed-carbon%, a coal with 60% fixed carbon has a calorific value of about:
questions.solution: CV ≈ 70 × 60 = 4200 kcal/kg (illustrative proxy).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Into which two broad types is the lustre of minerals classified in hand specimen study?
options: Only metallic lustre is exhibited by opaque ore minerals such as galena
Metallic (opaque) or non-metallic (vitreous, pearly, silky, earthy)
Body color alone determines the observed mineral lustre
Hardness controls whether a mineral appears dull or bright
questions.solution: Metallic: pyrite, galena. Vitreous: quartz. Pearly: talc. Silky: asbestos.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Specific storage (Ss) of an aquifer is defined as the volume of water released per:
options: The volume of water drained from storage in an aquifer under the pull of gravity alone during the pumping
The ratio of the saturated aquifer thickness to its specific yield value during tests
Volume released per unit volume per unit head change. Elastic (confined). Ss = ρg(α + nβ)
The volume of water released from a confined aquifer by the pull of gravity drainage alone
questions.solution: Ss: compressibility of water (β=4.4×10^-10 Pa^-1) and aquifer (α). Confined: S = Ss×b. Unconfined: S_y.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the chemical formula and structural type of biotite, a mica group mineral?
options: Framework silicate with three-dimensional SiO4 linkage
Tectosilicate structure identical to that of feldspar
Dioctahedral phyllosilicate with two Al per formula unit
questions.solution: Biotite: black mica. Trioctahedral (3 Mg/Fe per formula unit). Common in many rocks.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The capture zone of a pumping well is defined as the portion of the aquifer from which:
options: Volume of aquifer from which well draws water
The entire area of the aquifer basin feeding the river system
Only the physical volume of the borehole and the pump chamber
The region where water levels rise above the original static level
questions.solution: Capture zone: area of flow lines terminating at well.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A coal seam covers 5 km², is 2 m thick, with density 1.3 t/m³. The in-situ reserve is about:
questions.solution: Reserve = area×thickness×density = 5×10⁶ m²×2 m×1.3 t/m³ ≈ 13 Mt.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: A bed drops 30 m over a horizontal distance of 40 m. Its dip angle is about:
questions.solution: dip = tan⁻¹(rise/run) = tan⁻¹(30/40) ≈ 36.9°.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What streak colour does the mineral pyrite produce when rubbed on a streak plate?
questions.solution: Pyrite (FeS2) — brassy yellow, greenish-black streak. 'Fool's gold'.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The capillary fringe is the zone lying above the water table where water is held by:
options: Zone below the water table where all the pores are completely filled
Zone above water table where water is held by capillary forces. Saturation > 0
Thin dry layer at the surface that transmits no water to the roots
Saturated band located beneath the aquifer's impermeable confining bed layer at depth
questions.solution: Capillary rise: fine sand 1-2m, silt 2-5m, clay >10m. Negative pressure.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The specific yield (S_y) of an unconfined aquifer is defined as the:
options: Volume drained by gravity / total volume. Unconfined aquifer storage
Ratio of pore water held against gravity to the total volume
Volume of water released per unit surface area per unit head fall
Fraction of the total volume stored as water under confined pressure
questions.solution: S_y: sand 0.2-0.3, clay 0.02-0.05. S_y + S_r = porosity (S_r = specific retention).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What do load casts on the base of a sedimentary bed indicate about their formation?
options: Ridge-like projections found on the top surface of the sandstone bed
Irregular pods confined to the interior of a single thick massive bed
Bulbous projections on bottom of bed. Soft sediment deformation
Straight, parallel ridges aligned exactly with the bedding plane direction
questions.solution: Load cast: differential loading. Flute cast: current scour. Both sole marks (bottom of bed).

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which mining method typically produces a subsidence trough at the surface?
options: Subsidence only occurs at the mine portal and never above the extracted panel area
The ground surface always rises as an uplift dome over the panel
Longwall mining → subsidence trough. Angle of draw. Impact on structures
Roof falls underground are fully unrelated to any surface movement
questions.solution: Subsidence: vertical displacement. Tilt and curvature cause damage. Mitigation: backfill, pillars.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which landform is characteristic of the lower course of a river and is formed when a meander loop is cut off and abandoned?
questions.solution: Oxbow lakes form when a meander neck is breached and the loop is abandoned as a crescent-shaped lake; typical of floodplains in the lower course. Alluvial fans form at mountain fronts.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following is a method of artificial groundwater recharge?
options: Only riverbank filtration of surface water along the banks of the perennial rivers of the region
Check dams, recharge wells, percolation tanks, roof-top harvesting, injection wells
Only the pumping of groundwater from deep production wells during a prolonged drought period of the year
Only seawater intrusion barriers that are built along the coastal belt of the open sea
questions.solution: MAR: aquifer storage and recovery (ASR). Water quality treatment. Clogging management.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: The Permian–Triassic mass extinction is attributed mainly to which cause?
options: Siberian Traps volcanism and climate change
Asteroid impact at the K-Pg boundary layer
Global cooling associated with a major ice age
Rapid sea level fall on passive continental margins
questions.solution: P-T extinction: largest in Earth history. ~96% species lost. Caused by Siberian Traps: CO2, SO2, ozone depletion, ocean anoxia.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Ore reserve classification (JORC): indicated resource requires:
options: Sufficient exploration for geological confidence but lower than measured
Surface exposure of the orebody without any sampling carried out beneath it
No drilling, with tonnage estimated purely from regional geological extrapolation
Any level of confidence, including purely speculative regional analogies
questions.solution: Indicated: enough data for planning. Inferred: limited data. Measured: high confidence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following is a common rockfall protection measure?
options: Only the removal of the source block by controlled blasting of the cliff face
Only warning sirens with no physical protection measure at all
Only regrading of the slope to a gentler uniform angle
Barrier, catch ditch, mesh, rock bolt, shotcrete. Warning systems
questions.solution: Rockfall: netting (draped, anchored). Attenuator barriers. Risk: exposure × probability × consequence.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which mineral pair is the essential assemblage of the eclogite facies at very high pressure?
options: Garnet + omphacite. Very high P. Densest crustal rock (~3.5 g/cm³)
Amphibole-bearing assemblage that is stable at moderate pressures
Low-density quartz-feldspar rock formed at very shallow crustal depths
Hydrous mineral assemblage stable in shallow crustal levels
questions.solution: Eclogite: subduction zone. Coesite in UHP rocks. Diamond-grade: >4 GPa.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which of the following correctly describes pingos, their morphology and the two systems by which they form?
options: Cone-shaped hill built up by repeated eruptions of lava and pyroclastic material around a central volcanic vent
Ridge of wind-blown sand aligned with the prevailing wind direction in a desert region
Ice-cored mounds in permafrost. Open-system (groundwater) and closed-system (lake)
Ridge of unsorted debris deposited along the margin of a glacier during a period of retreat
questions.solution: Pingo: up to 100m high. Collapse pingo → thermokarst pond. Continuous permafrost zone.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: What is the relative duration of the Precambrian, Paleozoic, Mesozoic, and Cenozoic in the geological time scale?
options: All eras are of equal duration across the entire geological time scale of the Earth history
Precambrian is the shortest interval, covering less than 10% of Earth's recorded geological history
Precambrian (88%), Paleozoic (545-251 Ma), Mesozoic (251-66 Ma), Cenozoic (66 Ma-present)
Cenozoic is the longest era, spanning nearly half of the total Earth history span recorded
questions.solution: Hadean, Archean, Proterozoic (Precambrian). Phanerozoic: Paleo-Meso-Cenozoic.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: (U-Th)/He dating of apatite, with a helium closure temperature of about 70°C, is mainly used to study what?
options: Closure at a low temperature of about sixty to seventy degrees centigrade
He diffusion: closure temperature ~70°C. For exhumation studies
No dependence of the helium retention on temperature whatsoever at any depth
Very high closure temperature near three hundred degrees centigrade or more
questions.solution: AHe: low-T thermochronometer. (U-Th)/He age = time since cooling through ~70°C.

questions.stem: In coastal hydrogeology, the Ghyben-Herzberg relation is used to describe which feature of freshwater-saltwater systems?
options: Relationship between rainfall intensity and groundwater recharge
Variation of aquifer thickness with depth below the water table
Rate of seawater movement through a barrier island system
questions.solution: z = 40h. Freshwater head h corresponds to z depth of interface.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which regions of the electromagnetic spectrum, from visible through near-infrared to microwave, are used in remote sensing?
options: Only the visible and near-infrared portions of the spectrum
Only thermal infrared, used for temperature measurement
Visible (0.4-0.7 μm), NIR, SWIR, TIR, Microwave (radar)
Only microwave, which cannot sense optical properties
questions.solution: Multispectral: multiple bands. Hyperspectral: hundreds of narrow bands.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: In a standard False Colour Composite (FCC) displayed with NIR, Red and Green bands, healthy vegetation appears as which colour?
questions.solution: In FCC (NIR-Red-Green), healthy vegetation appears red because of its very high near-infrared reflectance; built-up areas appear cyan or grey.

questions.subject: Paper-II · Professional Knowledge
questions.stem: Which remote sensing techniques, passive and active, are commonly used to estimate soil moisture from space?
options: Using only optical NDVI vegetation indices, which can directly measure the root-zone water content
Using thermal inertia alone, as derived from a single daytime thermal image only
Passive microwave (L-band: SMOS, SMAP). Active (C-band: Sentinel-1). Optical/thermal
Using only ground-based gravimetry, with no spaceborne sensing involved at all
questions.solution: SMAP: L-band radiometer + radar. 3km, 2-3 day. Soil moisture + freeze/thaw. Surface ~5cm depth.
